chunks: And in it is that Amir al-Mu'minin asked my father (peace be upon him): 'A man prays while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) without performing ghusl; does his prayer suffice for him or not?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless he is on a journey or unable to perform ghusl.'

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, in the narration of his son)
key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمَعْمُونِ: Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him)
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Is a man's prayer valid if he prays in a state of junub without performing ghusl?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) ruling that major ritual impurity (*junub*) invalidates prayer unless a specific concession (*rukhsa*) applies, such as for travelers or those unable to perform *ghusl*. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the general obligation of purity and the practical exceptions derived from the Quranic verse of ablution (5:6), emphasizing that while *ghusl* is the norm, necessity permits prayer with dry ablution (*tayammum*) or even without it in extreme cases.
